text.en: Asha held a glass prism in sunlight and splashed a rainbow on the wall. "White light is a mixture of colours," said her teacher.

Light travels in straight lines called rays. When it passes obliquely from one medium to another it bends, which is refraction. The first law of refraction says the incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in the same plane, and the second is Snell's law: the ratio of sines of the angles is constant. The refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium.
A prism splits white light into seven colours, which is dispersion, because each colour has a different angle of refraction, with red bending least and violet most. Scattering of sunlight by atmospheric gases is Rayleigh scattering and explains the blue sky and red sunset.
Lenses are convex or concave, and the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, with magnification m = v/u and power P = 1/f in dioptres, describes the image. Convex lenses are used in magnifiers and cameras and concave lenses in correcting short sight. The human eye forms images on the retina. Defects such as myopia and hypermetropia are corrected using lenses. The microscope and telescope extend our sight.

prompt.en: A friend says The sky is blue because it reflects the sea. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Sky colour is due to scattering of sunlight.
